Um first you go to ubuntu.com and download the OS. It should have instructions on how to create a USB flash drive of that OS or a DVD of the OS. I prefer Linux Ubuntu cause it's noob friendly, but others like Linux mint. Ubuntu is a distro, which is like saying that Ubuntu is a flavor of linux. I know someone will disagree with me and provide a more in depth explanation but since you're new this is just fine. :D Now depending on how you installed it to the media(USB flash drive or DVD) you have a little bit of a complex method of installing it to the hard disk, but this is normal for newbies. First I want you to figure out how to get into your BIOS settings. On my computer when I press the ON button I have to press f11, your computer may be different. BIOS is what tells the OS to wake up and start doing work when you power it on. Move around in your BIOS inferface, but read very carefully the instructions presented to you by the BIOS to ensure you don't change anything yet. Some of the BIOS features are very advanced and should only be used by knowledgeable individual. Next, find the place where you change boot order. Boot is like saying "wake up order". The boot order will sequentially "activate" hardware devices where the OS could reside until it finds the one where the OS is actually residing. So lets assume you've set USB to be activated first. BIOS will then activate the Linux OS on your flash drive(USB) , follow the prompts on your screen to install linux. If you're stuck on a screen ask for help. I would have a knowledgeable Linux friend with you to help ease the installation process as it can be very treacherous for newbies. If you're doing this on your own a google search of the issue will generally produce results. Always make sure to have more than 1 internet capable device when installing linux just in case something doesn't work right.

If you've installed Linux properly an interface should appear asking what you want to start. it defaults to starting linux if you don't press anything.

Congratulations you have now installed the Linux distro of your choice. Enjoy.
